Oct 23, 18:36 UTC Monitoring - The degradation has been mitigated. We are monitoring to ensure stability. Oct 23, 17:27 UTC Update - Some Dependabot alerts continue to be delayed in closing after repository updates address a vulnerability. We're continuing to investigate and work to restore normal processing. Oct 23, 16:43 UTC Update - We’re continuing to investigate delays in some Dependabot alerts closing after affected repositories are updated. Alert processing remains backed up, and additional processing capacity is rolling out to help reduce the backlog. We’re monitoring progress and will share another update as we learn more. [1.22.0] 2026 10 15 [!IMPORTANT] Python 3.15 support: The core framework and root agent framework package now support Python 3.15, but not every package, optional extra, or feature supports it yet because of upstream dependency constraints. Before upgrading, check the README for each package and extra you use. The Python README summarizes the currently known limitations. [!WARNING] Persisted state compatibility: This applies to persisted artifacts that contain serialized Agent Framework Content or streamed response update records. That includes chat and message histories; session stores and protocol snapshots when they embed those records; and workflow checkpoints only when their checkpoint state contains them. Plain session metadata and checkpoints without serialized messages, content, or response updates are unaffected. The 1.22 runtime can read records written by earlier releases, but pre 1.22 runtimes cannot read new records containing hosted or merge mode . Do not run old and new workers against the same affected store during a rolling deployment, and do not downgrade after 1.22 has written these records unless the new state is isolated or migrated. Announcements / highlights Improved gateway reliability. Fixed stale backend connection reuse, TLS certificate initialization issues during gateway restarts, and false capacity related HTTP 429 responses. Internal health probes are no longer disrupted by capacity throttling or connection rebalancing. More flexible WebSocket routing and load balancing. Added wildcard and URL template matching for routing multiple paths through a single WebSocket API, plus support for distributing connections across backend pools. Enhanced backend certificate validation. Added SHA 256 and SHA 512 certificate thumbprints, issuer only pinning without a common name requirement, and matching against intermediate certificates in the available chain. Expanded messaging controls. Added configurable Event Hubs logging message size limits and Service Bus correlation ID, reply to, and scheduled enqueue time properties. More reliable caching and API updates. Fixed truncated cached responses and addressed API import/update failures involving operation ID changes and HTTP method/path conflicts. Stronger credential protection and request validation. Improved secret redaction in API exports and import errors, ti... - **[Elevated 404s for GitHub App s2s tokens in git/API](../../../knowledge/GitHub/updates/2026/github-status-history-github-358e5cb3af8a.md)** - github; `unknown` / `medium`. Oct 27, 08:00 UTC Resolved - Between 0655 and 0801 UTC on 10/27, customers experienced increased failure rates for API and git requests authenticated with server-to-server tokens for GitHub Apps (excluding Actions tokens). During this window, authenticated git operations mistakenly returned 404 for 1.24% (2.6x) of requests on average and 2.49% (5.3x) at peak. These failures were caused by a scheduled maintenance event where GitHub migrated 7 tables between two MySQL clusters in our IAD and Azure Central US datacenters. One of the affected tables stores installation records for GitHub App server-to-server tokens (excluding Actions). We've successfully completed several of these migrations in recent months without notable customer impact. However, in this case, the migration coincided with a scheduled cleanup job on the installation records table, which deleted approximately 59 million records from 0444-0617 UTC. As a result, the gh-ost tooling used in the migration experienced inter-cluster replication delays (up to 1 hour at peak). At 0655 UTC, we begin transitioning reads of the target tables to the new MySQL cluster, with 100% of reads cutover at 0721 UTC. Customer impact bega... [Source](https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/dnslv7xdl4fj)

Oct 19, 16:56 UTC Resolved - On October 19, 2026, between 15:24 and 16:52 UTC, GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages, and webhooks generated by Actions were degraded. Live updates on GitHub.com and code search were also degraded for part of this time. No data was lost. Impact - Workflow status updates, logs, and checks were delayed. - 5.13% of jobs on GitHub-hosted runners were delayed in starting, and 0.02% of workflow runs failed. - During the first 30 minutes, 8.47% of requests to the Actions jobs REST API returned errors. Pages deployments and webhooks generated by Actions runs were delayed. An internal Actions service that stores logs and run status lost connections to some of its cache servers in one cloud region and immediately retried them from every server at once. The resulting surge of new connections overloaded a shared network link between our data center and that region, which also disrupted other services that use the same link. We mitigated the incident by moving the Actions service off the affected cache servers and reducing connections from other services on the link. We then processed the delayed Actions work. - **[Incident with Actions, Pull Requests and Issues](../../../knowledge/GitHub/updates/2026/github-status-history-github-20e2c3e7f188.md)** - github; `unknown` / `medium`. Oct 12, 20:16 UTC Resolved - On October 12th 2026 11:51 UTC GitHub experienced elevated 500 responses across several application pages. This caused failures on Issues and Pull Requests as well as Projects and Actions. Customers also experienced delayed notifications in their web inbox and via email. The immediate impact to Issues, Pull Requests, Projects, and Actions was mitigated by 12:41 UTC on October 12th. Notifications deliveries to the web inbox and via email were recovering at 15:27 UTC and fully mitigated by 20:16 UTC. The incident was triggered through a latent condition in our notifications delivery pipeline that put a high volume of an expensive query on our sharded database replicas. This reduced available database capacity to serve requests for Issues, Pull Requests, Projects, and Actions. We have fixed the notifications pipeline’s code path that issued the expensive query. We are also improving resilience of the database layer to reduce the likelihood and impact of similar incidents. - **[Delayed Actions status check results](../../../knowledge/GitHub/updates/2026/github-status-history-github-117a00ab8225.md)** - github; `unknown` / `low`. Oct 23, 08:05 UTC Resolved - On October 23, 2026, between 07:06 UTC and 07:27 UTC, GitHub Actions workflow run results were delayed. Job status, check run updates, and logs in the GitHub UI and API updated with an average delay of about 2 minutes, and some updates were delayed by up to about 7 minutes. During this window, a storage dependency that Actions uses to process workflow logs and artifacts throttled our requests. This slowed result processing, causing updates to queue up. The queue was fully processed by 07:27 UTC, shortly after the throttling stopped. To reduce the risk of recurrence, we have added several storage accounts to increase capacity, and we are working on additional steps to continue to scale. We are also working with our storage provider to understand why the throttling occurred, and improving how result processing handles storage throttling and how quickly we detect it. Oct 23, 07:56 UTC Update - As of 07:27 UTC, Actions results are delivering within normal SLOs again. Thank you for this patience during this period of delayed Actions results delivery. Our team continues to monitor system health and explore refinements to reduce impact to customers in the f... [Source](https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/ntrfd2jqldn6)
